The most common running injuries are overuse injuries: runner's knee, shin splints, Achilles tendinopathy and plantar fasciitis. They usually come from increasing mileage too quickly, not from a single bad step. Strength training for calves, hips and glutes reduces risk, as does rotating shoes and keeping most runs easy. Pain that changes your stride is a reason to stop. Returning after an injury means walking and running intervals and rebuilding volume gradually, the same slow progression as in [[Easy runs and heart rate]].
